item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Aug. 23)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Gallery: Photos of the Week
item.description: "Sunday Morning" looks at some of the most evocative images captured the week of August 16-22, 2026.

item.title: The real no-shoes Kenny Chesney
item.description: In his recent memoir, "Heart Life Music," Kenny Chesney describes his life's journey, from Knoxville, Tenn., to No Shoes Nation and beyond. Chesney sits down with Lee Cowan in the Florida Keys, where the country superstar is just another laid-back local, to talk about family, touring, and how he recovered from a 2009 concert which he describes as "hitting a wall." [Originally broadcast Oct. 26, 2025.]

item.title: Iran's president defends U.S. memorandum of understanding as best path forward
item.description: The new head of Iran's supreme national security council issued the warning to countries who join the U.S.'s economic war on Tehran.

item.title: Inside shooting victim Fletcher Merkel's bedroom
item.description: Eight-year-old Fletcher Merkel was one of two students killed when a gunman fired randomly into the Annunciation Catholic Church in Minneapolis last August. Steve Hartman (who documented the bedrooms of young shooting victims in the Oscar-winning short documentary "All the Empty Rooms") talked with Fletcher's parents, Jesse and Mollie, about their son, and the sacred space he left behind. [For more, visit cbsnews.com/rooms]

item.title: Milan's Casa Verdi, a rest home for musicians living in harmony
item.description: Opera great Giuseppe Verdi, one of history's most successful composers, used his fortune to create a retirement home for professional musicians "not favored by fortune." Residents of Casa Verdi in Milan not only share their lifetimes of artistry, they also provide master classes to young musicians. Chris Livesay reports.

item.title: Passage: In memoriam
item.description: "Sunday Morning" remembers some of the notable figures who left us this week, including actress Hayden Panettiere, star of "Nashville" and "Heroes."

item.title: From the ashes arise origami koi
item.description: Robert Lang, a physicist who became a leading figure in the world of origami, lost a lifetime's work of folded paper art to the 2025 wildfires in Altadena, Calif. He then set out to recreate his designs – and the origami community joined in.

item.title: From the ashes arise origami koi
item.description: In the 1990s, Robert Lang, a physicist who once designed lasers for NASA, became a leading figure in the world of origami, combining math and art to create magic. After the 2025 Altadena wildfire destroyed his house, and a lifetime's works of folded paper, Lang set out to recreate his designs – and the origami community joined in. Tracy Smith reports.

item.title: Capturing an immortal photograph of jazz legends
item.description: In 1958, photographer Art Kane assembled many of the greatest legends in jazz on a brownstone stoop in Harlem; his picture became one of the most famous images ever taken of artistic royalty. Correspondent Mo Rocca talks about Kane's iconic group portrait with the photographer's son, Jonathan; and about the legacy the musicians left behind with legendary bassist Ron Carter, who played alongside nearly all of the jazz greats pictured that hot August day.

item.title: Fast-growing Hawk Fire near Reno, Nevada forces thousands to evacuate
item.description: The fire apparently began Saturday and grew significantly throughout the day, fueled by strong, gusty winds, low humidity and dry vegetation.

item.title: Luna Parc: A home, and an eclectic canvas
item.description: For more than 35 years, artist Ricky Boscarino has turned his house in Sandyston, N.J., and its 8.5 acres into an eye-popping gallery filled with sculptures, ceramics, mosaics and whimsy. Correspondent Serena Altschul pays a visit to Boscarino's quirky home, dubbed Luna Parc, and his outdoor "electric garden."

item.title: Almanac: August 23
item.description: "Sunday Morning" looks back at historical events on this date.

item.title: The explosion of ticks and Alpha-gal syndrome
item.description: This year, ER visits for tick bites have increased dramatically, corresponding with a new threat: a rise in Alpha-gal syndrome (AGS), where one bite from a lone star tick can make you violently allergic to red meat. How can you best avoid tick bites?

item.title: Tropical Storm Moke expected to bring up to 15 inches of rain in Hawaii
item.description: Hawaii is still cleaning up from Hurricane Lala, which dumped massive amounts of rain on the islands.

item.title: The explosion of ticks and Alpha-gal syndrome
item.description: This year, emergency room visits for tick bites have increased dramatically, corresponding with a new threat: a rise in Alpha-gal syndrome (AGS), where one bite from a lone star tick can make you violently allergic to red meat. Correspondent David Pogue looks at how residents of Martha Vineyard are addressing an epidemic of Alpha-gal, and talks with experts about how best to avoid tick bites.

item.title: Mexican official accused by U.S. of drug trafficking abruptly resigns again
item.description: Sinaloa Gov. Ruben Rocha Moya is accused of allegedly colluding with the infamous Sinaloa Cartel to distribute drugs inside the U.S.

item.title: IndyCar is holding its first race in D.C. today. Here's what to know.
item.description: Twenty-five cars traveling at top speeds approaching 180 mph are zooming around the National Mall this weekend as IndyCar takes over downtown D.C.

item.title: Zelenskyy rejects wartime elections, cites "huge risk"
item.description: After Ukraine's fired defense minister publicly called for wartime elections, Zelenskyy said it would risk splitting the country.

item.title: Canada says it will begin retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods after Labor Day
item.description: The U.S. and Canada have wrangled for decades over trade, and somehow, they still managed to remain friends, allies and trading partners.

item.title: "48 Hours" show schedule
item.description: True crime. Real justice. To miss it would be a crime.

item.title: Truck computer contains clues to motive in murder, prosecutors say
item.description: The state argues an "infotainment system" is a window into the brain of a South Carolina man who mowed down his estranged wife's boyfriend.

item.title: The Hit-and-Run Homicide of Davis McClendon
item.description: A romance is cut short when a man is found dead near his mangled car. His newfound love is convinced it was no accident. "48 Hours" correspondent Anne-Marie Green reports.

item.title: Chinese humanoid robot beats Usain Bolt's sprint world record
item.description: Two human records were smashed by robots competing in the Olympics-like World Humanoid Robot Games in China.

item.title: Judge denies Karmelo Anthony's appeal for a new trial in killing of Austin Metcalf
item.description: The decision comes after both prosecutors and Anthony's new defense team revealed more details in a tense two-day hearing.

item.title: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll considering stepping down, sources say
item.description: U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is considering stepping down from his post by the end of the year, two people familiar with the matter told CBS News Saturday.

item.title: How an oil trail led to suspect in South Carolina hit-and-run homicide
item.description: A trail of clues — including an oil leak, security video and data from a truck's onboard computer — lead S.C. investigators to a jealous man suspected of running down a romantic rival.

item.title: Frustration mounts for thousands still without power after deadly Indiana storms
item.description: Several days of powerful storms walloped northwest Indiana, killing at least seven people and displacing about 1,000. The storms brought record rainfall that flooded several communities.

item.title: Russian and Ukrainian attacks kill at least 10 after deadly mall drone strike
item.description: The attacks come a day after a two-wave drone strike on a shopping mall in Zelenskyy's hometown killed 16 people.

item.title: Supreme Court temporarily allows work on White House ballroom to continue
item.description: Chief Justice John Roberts issued a stay that will remain in place until the Supreme Court takes further action.
